01 — PROCESSHow I work

A simple, repeatable process — it always starts with the requirement and the business questions, and ends with a dashboard someone can actually use to decide.

01

Understand the Requirement

Start by listening — what decision is needed, who will use the analysis, and what "good" looks like for them.

Stakeholder NeedGoal Setting
02

Define the Business Problem & Questions

Frame the business problem and the questions the data must answer — exactly how my retail capstone began, with a problem statement and business questions BQ1–BQ8.

Problem StatementBusiness Questions
03

Collect the Data

Only then gather the source data the questions call for — files, tables and exports that can actually answer them.

ExcelSQLCSV
04

Clean & Prepare

Fix formats, remove duplicates and inconsistencies, and shape messy data into a reliable, analysis-ready table — checking totals as I go.

Power QueryPandasValidation
05

Analyse & Build the Dashboard

Explore the data, model it, build the KPI measures, and present the findings as an interactive dashboard.

Power BIDAXPivot Tables
06

Share Insights & Recommendations

Close with what the numbers mean — clear insights and practical recommendations the business can act on.

InsightsRecommendationsKPI Reporting

03 — PORTFOLIOProjects

Three end-to-end projects — from a business problem and cleaned data through to KPI dashboards and recommendations. Project 1 is my Entri final capstone, built across Excel, MySQL, Python and Power BI.

Project 1 · Capstone · Excel · MySQL · Python · Power BI

Retail Business Performance & Profitability Analytics

End-to-end analysis of 10,000 retail orders (2024–2025) for a multi-city retail chain scenario — starting from a business problem: sales were growing, but profit was leaking. Analysed discount impact, category and store profitability, customer segments and returns, and delivered a 3-page Power BI dashboard.

  • Headline results: Sales ₹11.37 Cr · Profit ₹1.99 Cr · Overall margin 17.52% — cross-verified in Excel, SQL, Python and Power BI.
  • Discount leak: Discount vs margin correlation −0.87; orders discounted above 30% ran at a −15.97% margin, and 14.8% of order lines were loss-making.
  • Built it end to end: Excel workbook with 5 PivotTables, PivotCharts and 3 slicers; MySQL analysis (BQ1–BQ8); Python EDA with Pandas and 5 charts; Power BI model with 12 DAX measures and 3 dashboard pages — Executive Overview, Profitability & Discount, and Stores, Customers & Returns.
  • Recommendation: Cap routine discounts at 20%, rethink festive-season discounting, and rank stores on margin — not just sales.
